notes: RS-25 sea level, 15 deg cone (before): mass flow 262.1 kg/s, C_f 1.7624, c* 4738.8 m/s, exit Mach 1.488 (area-avg) at step 5511 (253 x 415 cells, Compact plume, floors 665). SNAPSHOT OF AN UNSTEADY LIMIT CYCLE, not a steady state — see the rs25-sea-level-unsteady note.

RS-25 sea level, 80% bell (after): mass flow 392.9 kg/s, C_f 1.5175, c* 3145.6 m/s, exit Mach 2.405 (area-avg) at step 5511 (224 x 415 cells, Compact plume, floors 0). SNAPSHOT OF AN UNSTEADY LIMIT CYCLE, not a steady state — see the rs25-sea-level-unsteady note.

RS-25 at sea level is deeply overexpanded (p_e/p_a ~ 0.085, §13 separation-warning regime) and has NO steady state in this inviscid model: a 30k-step probe of both contours shows the shock system breathing in and out of the nozzle, with exit-plane readouts oscillating over mdot 291-738 kg/s (cone) / 48-895 (bell), exit Mach 0.58-2.97 / 0.77-3.59, C_f 1.41-1.86 / 1.43-1.79. The cone-vs-bell C_f comparison is therefore asserted at 20 km (attached flow), not at sea level.
RS-25 at 20 km, 15 deg cone (before): mass flow 492.3 kg/s, C_f 1.6789, c* 2523.3 m/s, exit Mach 4.011 (area-avg) at step 5511 (253 x 415 cells, Compact plume, floors 1495).
RS-25 at 20 km, 80% bell (after): mass flow 494.1 kg/s, C_f 1.7007, c* 2501.8 m/s, exit Mach 4.178 (area-avg) at step 5511 (224 x 415 cells, Compact plume, floors 0).

Raptor 2 exit angle NOT reproduced and not asserted: Rao table gives theta_e = 9.48 deg at eps 34.3 / 75.6% bell vs ~6.0 deg inferred from published geometry (a 6 deg exit sits on the table's 90% row). The real contour is a custom optimisation, not a Rao bell, and the table is digitised at gamma 1.23-1.25 vs Raptor's 1.16.
